question: Who founded the Servants of India Society to promote national education and social reforms in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was a prominent leader of the Indian freedom struggle and a key figure in the early 20th century Indian political landscape.
 
• He founded the **Servants of India Society** in **1905** with the aim of promoting education, social reform, and the upliftment of Indian society.
 
• The society's key objectives included training Indians to work for the betterment of the country and addressing issues like poverty, illiteracy, and social discrimination. *Hence, the correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.*
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was also a mentor to **Mahatma Gandhi**, who considered him a guide and inspiration in his early political career.
 
• The Servants of India Society emphasized selfless service and dedication to the nation, which was reflected in its members' commitment to work for the underprivileged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**

 
 
• He was born on **May 9, 1866,** in **Ratnagiri district, Maharashtra**.
 
• He was a moderate leader in the **Indian National Congress**, advocating constitutional methods and dialogue with the British to achieve reforms.
 
• He served as the president of the Indian National Congress in **1905**.
 
• Gokhale was an advocate of social reform, particularly in the areas of education, public health, and the removal of untouchability.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society:**
 
 
• The society was headquartered in **Pune, Maharashtra**.
 
• Its members were required to take a vow of lifelong dedication to the service of India.
 
• The organization focused on educating the masses, promoting Indian self-reliance, and addressing social inequalities.
 
• It also provided a platform for training and nurturing leaders for the Indian freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **Other leaders mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• **S. N. Banerjee:** He was a prominent nationalist leader and one of the founders of the **Indian National Association**, but he did not establish the Servants of India Society.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** Known as the "Father of Indian Unrest," Tilak was a radical leader in the freedom movement and focused on Swaraj (self-rule), but he was not related to the Servants of India Society.
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal:** A key leader of the extremist faction in the Indian National Congress, Pal advocated for complete independence but was not associated with the Servants of India Society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Objectives of the Servants of India Society:**

 
 
• To provide education and improve literacy rates among Indians to empower them for self-governance.
 
• To work for the eradication of social evils like untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
• To promote public health and hygiene through awareness campaigns and services.
 
• To encourage Indians to work selflessly for the progress of the country.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Gokhale's Leadership:**
 
 
• Gokhale's moderate approach laid the foundation for constitutional reforms like the **Indian Councils Act of 1909** (Morley-Minto Reforms).
 
• He inspired future leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi** to adopt non-violent means for achieving freedom.
